title: Military Rule and the Return to Democracy in Nigeria

blocks.text: Nigeria's political landscape has been shaped significantly by military interventions, which have often disrupted democratic governance.

blocks.markdown: Military rule in Nigeria began shortly after independence in 1960, with the first coup occurring in 1966. The military justified its intervention by citing political instability, corruption, and ethnic tensions as reasons for their takeover.

blocks.title: Military Intervention
blocks.text: Military intervention refers to the act of a country's armed forces taking control of the government, often justified by claims of restoring order and stability.

blocks.markdown: The features of military rule include centralized power, suspension of the constitution, and the use of force to suppress dissent. However, military regimes often face weaknesses such as lack of legitimacy, human rights abuses, and economic mismanagement.

blocks.title: Analyzing Military Rule
blocks.prompt: Identify the reasons for military intervention in Nigeria's politics.

steps.text: 1. Political instability and corruption were rampant in the early years post-independence.
2. Ethnic tensions and conflicts led to a lack of trust in civilian governments.

blocks.answer: The military intervened due to political instability, corruption, and ethnic tensions.

blocks.markdown: The transition to democracy in Nigeria involved several programs, including the establishment of a new constitution and the organization of elections. Notable transitions occurred in 1999 when General Abdulsalami Abubakar handed over power to a civilian government.

blocks.title: Exam Tip
blocks.text: When discussing military rule, always highlight both the justifications provided by the military and the consequences of their governance.

points: Military rule in Nigeria was often justified by claims of restoring order amidst political chaos.
The transition back to democracy involved significant constitutional reforms and elections.
